claims.content: To modify personal details, billing and shipping addresses, payment methods, and email notification preferences.
Customer
The Customer has a registered account in the system.
The Customer is currently signed in (authenticated) to the system.
The Customer's account status is active (i.e., the account is not closed or suspended).
The Customer has agreed to the Terms of Use Agreement.
The Customer is on the 'My Account' page or has navigated to an 'My Account Edit' page.
The system is displaying the Customer's current account information (e.g., First Name, Last Name, Member ID, E-mail, Phone, Password).
The Customer clicks the EDIT button on the 'My Information' section of the 'My Account' page to access the account editing interface.
The Customer is viewing the 'My Account' page with their current account information (First Name, Last Name, Member ID, E-mail, Phone, Password) displayed.
The Customer views their current account details displayed on the 'My Account' page, including First Name, Last Name, Member 'Handle', E-mail Address, Phone Number, and Password.
The Customer clicks the EDIT button/link to navigate to the 'My Account Edit page 1' to modify personal information.

The system displays the 'My Information' section with First Name, Last Name, Handle, and E-mail Address pre-populated, while Phone Number, New Password, and Verify Password fields are available for input.
The Customer enters data into the Phone Number, New Password, and Verify Password fields to update their account details.
The Customer clicks the EDIT button/link to navigate to the 'My Account Edit page 2' to modify address information.

The system displays the 'My Billing Address' and 'My Shipping Address' sections, showing current addresses and providing input fields for Address 1, Address 2, Suite/Apt, City, State, Zip Code, and Country.
The Customer populates the fields for the 'My New Billing Address' with the desired address information.
The Customer either populates the 'My New Shipping Address' fields manually or selects the 'Same as Billing Address' checkbox to auto-fill the shipping details.
The system performs address validation and improvement using a Core web service to check the entered addresses.
The Customer selects a default shipping method preference from the radio buttons, choosing either 'USPS Standard' or 'Expedited (5-day, add $5.00)'.

The Customer navigates to the payment method section, where they review existing payment methods (PayPal, Amazon, or Credit Card) and may update the credit card number or expiration date in the input fields.
The Customer interacts with the 'My Email Preferences' section, toggling checkboxes to enable or disable notifications for being outbid, winning an auction, and shipping of winnings.
The Customer clicks the 'Save Changes' button to commit the modifications to the account settings.

The system updates the account information, displays a pop-up message instructing the user to add 'shop@jewelryTV.rsys1.com' to their address book or safe senders list, and instructs the user to enable cookies in their web browser to ensure the site functions correctly.

Diverges from Step 11 (Payment Method Update): If the Customer chooses to register for PayPal or Amazon Payments instead of using a credit card, they click the respective link (e.g., 'sign up for a free PayPal account'). The system opens the payment provider's website in a separate browser instance or window, diverging from the standard form entry flow.

Diverges from Step 12 (Email Preferences): If the Customer has selected PayPal or Amazon as their default payment method, the system grayes out the 'outbid' and 'winner' notification checkboxes. The Customer cannot de-select these boxes; they remain checked by default and are locked.

Diverges from Step 13 (Save Changes): Instead of clicking 'Save Changes', the Customer clicks the red 'Cancel' button on the edit page. The system aborts the changes, discards any new data entered, and returns the Customer to the 'My Account' page.

Diverges from Step 13 (Save Changes): If the Customer intends to remove an existing payment method, they check the 'Delete this card from this account' checkbox for the specific card. Upon clicking 'Save Changes', the system removes that card from their account file.

Diverges from Step 11 (Payment Method Update): If the system detects that the Customer's default payment method is a credit card that has expired, the system displays a DIV layer prompting the user to enter a new credit card. The user is presented with two options: clicking 'Yes' navigates to the 'My Account Edit page 3' and the 'Manage Account Settings' use case terminates (redirecting to the 'Manage Payment Methods' flow or sub-use case), while clicking 'No' navigates to the home page and the use case terminates.

Diverges from Step 13 (Save Changes): If the Customer attempts to save changes to 'My Information' or 'My New Information' but fails to enter their current password, the system prevents the update of other account fields and displays the error message: 'Error: Current Password is required to update your account information.' The Customer remains on the page to correct the input.

Diverges from Step 9 (Address Validation): If the Core web service returns address correction suggestions or rejects the address due to validation errors, the system displays these suggestions or error messages to the Customer, preventing the save until the address is corrected.

Diverges from Step 11 (Payment Method Update): If the system encounters an error or unexpected condition while processing the payment information (e.g., invalid card details or processing failure), it displays a warning note: 'Please note: Your billing address information must be entered exactly as it appears on your credit card statement to avoid delays in processing your order.' The Customer must correct the billing address or card details.
The system saves all modifications made to membership account information, billing/shipping addresses, payment methods, and email preferences.
The user is returned to the 'My Account' page.

The system displays a pop-up message instructing the user to add 'shop@jewelryTV.rsys1.com' to their address book or safe senders list to ensure delivery of outbid, winner, and product shipment notification emails.
The system displays a pop-up message instructing the user to enable cookies in their web browser to ensure the site functions correctly.
The system triggers an automated 'transactional' email containing a 'Thank You' message, with instructions to enable cookies and add the sender's email to the safe senders list.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] The 'trigger' slot is empty. Main Flow Step 1 describes the Customer viewing current account details. Without a defined trigger, it is unclear what initiates the 'Manage Account Settings' use case. Typically, the trigger would be 'Customer selects to modify account settings' or 'Customer accesses My Account page'. The current preconditions list includes an action (PC-007 'clicks EDIT') which arguably belongs in a trigger or early main flow step, creating confusion. The empty trigger breaks the continuity with the main flow's start. (slot empty/missing)

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The main flow (Step 2) explicitly states that clicking the EDIT button navigates the Customer to a 'My Account Edit page 1'. This navigation implies a transition between distinct views or URLs. However, the Preconditions do not assert that the system supports this navigation or that the 'My Account Edit page' is accessible. A precondition is missing to ensure the target page exists and is reachable from the current state.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 0 describes a branch where clicking 'Yes' navigates to 'My Account Edit page 3' and the use case terminates, while clicking 'No' navigates to the home page. While termination is a valid exit, the description is ambiguous about whether 'My Account Edit page 3' is a new use case, a sub-flow, or a continuation. More critically, the claim states the use case terminates in both branches, but the navigation to 'My Account Edit page 3' implies a potential handoff or continuation of settings management that isn't clearly defined as a terminal state in the context of the current use case 'Manage Account Settings'. If page 3 is part of the same use case, the exit is missing. If it's a different use case, the handoff should be explicit. However, the most critical issue is that the exception flow claim says the use case terminates, but the navigation to a new page suggests the user is still within the system's account management context, potentially violating the clear exit requirement if that page belongs to another use case without a proper handoff description.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 2 describes a scenario where address validation fails. The system displays suggestions or error messages, 'preventing the save until the address is corrected.' This implies the user remains on the page to correct the input. However, it does not explicitly state what happens after the correction. Does the user re-click 'Save'? Does the system auto-retry? The rule requires a clear exit (return to a Main Flow step, terminate, or handoff). Staying in an error loop without a defined next step (like 'return to Step 7') is an incomplete exit definition.

inconsistency_hints: The goal statement includes 'To change membership account information' which is semantically distinct from the main flow's scope. The main flow explicitly lists 'Member Handle' as a displayed but not editable attribute (Step 1, 3). The flow allows editing of 'personal information' (Name, Email) and 'account settings' (Addresses, Payment, Preferences), but the term 'membership account information' is broader and potentially conflates with membership-level attributes (like tier or status) that are not modified in this flow. This represents a slight scope ambiguity where the goal implies a breadth of change that the main flow does not fully support for all 'membership' attributes.

The trigger is missing from the use case definition. While the Main Flow describes the actor clicking an 'EDIT' button, a standard Cockburn use case requires an explicit Trigger entry (typically 'Actor clicks EDIT' or 'Actor requests to modify account') to serve as the starting point for the flow. Without a defined trigger, the precondition 'Customer is on the My Account page' does not have a specific initiating event to activate the use case, breaking the vertical flow continuity.

The 'trigger' slot is empty. According to the 'main_flow' (Step 1), the process begins with the Customer viewing current account details. The 'preconditions' list does not include a state that establishes the system is on the 'My Account' page and displaying this information *before* any user interaction. While PC-006 mentions the customer is on the page, PC-007 describes an action ('clicks EDIT') which is a trigger-like event, not a pre-state. The precondition should describe the static state (Viewing Account Info) that allows the subsequent main flow steps to proceed logically, or the Trigger should be defined to capture the transition from viewing to editing. Given the main flow starts with viewing, a precondition asserting 'The Customer is viewing the My Account page' is missing or ambiguous.

Main Flow Step 14 states the system returns the customer to the 'My Account' page and updates information. However, Postconditions include specific pop-up messages (PO-000, PO-001) regarding email safe senders and browser cookies. Step 14 does not explicitly mention the system displaying these pop-ups or instructions. There is a gap in the main flow where these postcondition behaviors are not triggered or described.

Alternative flow claim 0 states it diverges from Step 11 (Payment Method Update). However, Step 11 in the main flow describes reviewing existing payment methods and updating credit card details. The alternative flow describes registering for PayPal or Amazon Payments, which is a distinct action (opening a new browser instance to a provider site) that is not a simple branch of the standard form entry described in Step 11. More critically, Step 11 does not mention PayPal/Amazon links as part of the standard flow to diverge from; it only mentions updating credit card numbers. The divergence implies Step 11 should have included these options or that this is a separate flow, but the linkage 'diverges from Step 11' is structurally weak if Step 11 doesn't offer those paths.

Exception flow claim 0 describes a divergence from Step 11 where the system displays a DIV layer. The user is given two options: clicking 'Yes' navigates to 'My Account Edit page 3' and clicking 'No' navigates to the home page. The flow does not define how the use case resumes or exits after these navigation events. Navigating to a different page ('My Account Edit page 3') or 'home page' typically terminates the current use case instance, but the exception flow does not explicitly state that the use case terminates or hand off to another use case. Without an explicit exit condition (e.g., 'terminate use case' or 'redirect to page X'), the exit coverage is ambiguous.
